name: The earth kasiṇa (pathavī-kasiṇa)
method_summary: Gazing at a prepared disk of dawn-coloured clay (or a ploughed field/threshing floor for one with past practice), the meditator repeats its name and adverts to it with eyes open and closed until the learning sign arises, then develops it away from the device until the counterpart sign and access appear, extends the sign, and reaches the four (Abhidhamma: five) jhānas; used as a basis for supernormal power (the basis for powers such as becoming many and walking on water).

warnings.text: Keep to a suitable dwelling, food, company and posture, or the sign is lost.

equivalents.note: concentration on the elements in the Yoga/haṭha catalogue; different theory and goal

name: Contemplation of the bloated corpse (uddhumātaka)
method_summary: The meditator goes to a corpse of this kind, having informed the senior monk and noted the route, grasps the sign in eleven ways with open eyes, develops the learning and counterpart signs and reaches the first jhāna; it counteracts lust and suits the greedy temperament.

warnings.text: A body of the opposite sex is unsuitable for the beginner; take precautions against dangers at charnel grounds (wild animals, non-human beings) and against fear.

equivalents.note: the sutta practice of foulness (U36); the Visuddhimagga's ten corpse-subjects are one of its forms

name: Recollection of the Buddha (buddhānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting the Buddha's special qualities ('accomplished, fully enlightened …') until the mind is filled with faith and gladness; reaches access.

name: Recollection of the Dhamma (dhammānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting the qualities of the Dhamma ('well proclaimed, visible here and now, timeless …'); reaches access.

name: Recollection of the Saṅgha (saṅghānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting the qualities of the community of noble disciples; reaches access.

name: Recollection of virtue (sīlānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting one's own virtue as unbroken and untarnished; reaches access.

name: Recollection of generosity (cāgānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting one's own generosity, free from the stain of avarice; reaches access.

name: Recollection of deities (devatānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting one's own faith, virtue, learning, generosity and understanding with the deities as witnesses; reaches access.

name: Recollection of peace (upasamānussati)
method_summary: Recollecting the qualities of nibbāna — the disillusionment of vanity, elimination of thirst, termination of the round, cessation; reaches access and suits the intelligent.

name: Mindfulness of death (maraṇassati)
method_summary: Attending wisely 'death will take place, the life faculty will be cut off'; if that is not enough, recollecting death in eight ways — as a murderer, as the ruin of success, by comparison, as sharing the body with many, as life's frailty, as signless, as the limited span, as the shortness of the moment; reaches access.

warnings.text: Recollecting the death of a loved one arouses sorrow, of an enemy gladness, of a stranger no urgency, and of oneself anxiety — so one attends wisely, not in these ways.

notes: The warning about wrong attention recalled from memory.

name: Mindfulness occupied with the body (kāyagatāsati)
method_summary: Learning the thirty-two parts by verbal and mental recitation in sets (skin pentad etc.), then attending to them by colour, shape, direction, location and delimitation as repulsive, until one part appears clearly and the first jhāna arises.

equivalents.note: the sutta contemplation of the thirty-two parts (U36)

name: Mindfulness of breathing (ānāpānasati)
method_summary: The commentarial method: counting the breaths, then connection (following), contact at the nostril tip or upper lip, fixing, until the counterpart sign appears and jhāna follows; then observing, turning away, purification (insight, path, fruit) and looking back (reviewing); all sixteen bases can carry one to arahantship.
signs_of_progress: counterpart sign (star, gem, cotton, smoke, cloud …)

warnings.text: Mindfulness of breathing is a subject for great persons, difficult to develop; the breath becomes very subtle, and the meditator must not give up but seek it where it touches.

name: Loving-kindness (mettā-bhāvanā)
method_summary: Developed first towards oneself, then a dear person, a neutral one and an enemy, dealing with resentment by reflection, until the barriers break down and the sign and access arise; then extended in all directions; reaches three (fourfold count) jhānas.

warnings.text: Guard against the near enemy, which resembles the virtue, and the far enemy, its opposite.

equivalents.note: YS 1.33's maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā as attitudes for calming the mind; the Visuddhimagga develops them to absorption

name: Compassion (karuṇā-bhāvanā)
method_summary: Developed first towards one in misery, then the dear, neutral and hostile; its near enemy is home-based grief, its far enemy cruelty.

warnings.text: Guard against the near enemy, which resembles the virtue, and the far enemy, its opposite.

equivalents.note: YS 1.33's maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā as attitudes for calming the mind; the Visuddhimagga develops them to absorption

name: Gladness (muditā-bhāvanā)
method_summary: Rejoicing in others' success, starting with a very dear companion; its near enemy is home-based joy, its far enemy aversion.

warnings.text: Guard against the near enemy, which resembles the virtue, and the far enemy, its opposite.

equivalents.note: YS 1.33's maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā as attitudes for calming the mind; the Visuddhimagga develops them to absorption

name: Equanimity (upekkhā-bhāvanā)
method_summary: Developed after the third jhāna of the other three, looking on beings as owners of their kamma; reaches the fourth jhāna; near enemy the equanimity of unknowing, far enemies greed and resentment.

warnings.text: Guard against the near enemy, which resembles the virtue, and the far enemy, its opposite.

equivalents.note: YS 1.33's maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā as attitudes for calming the mind; the Visuddhimagga develops them to absorption

name: The base of infinite space (ākāsānañcāyatana)
method_summary: Removing the kasiṇa sign and attending to the space it occupied as 'infinite space'. Preceded by mastery of the fourth jhāna on a kasiṇa.
prerequisites: fourth (fifth) jhāna on a kasiṇa with mastery

name: The base of infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatana)
method_summary: Attending to the consciousness that pervaded the space as 'infinite consciousness'. Preceded by mastery of the fourth jhāna on a kasiṇa.
prerequisites: fourth (fifth) jhāna on a kasiṇa with mastery

name: The base of nothingness (ākiñcaññāyatana)
method_summary: Attending to the absence of that consciousness as 'there is nothing'. Preceded by mastery of the fourth jhāna on a kasiṇa.
prerequisites: fourth (fifth) jhāna on a kasiṇa with mastery

name: The base of neither perception nor non-perception
method_summary: Attending to the base of nothingness as peaceful, until a state arises so subtle that perception can be said neither to be nor not to be. Preceded by mastery of the fourth jhāna on a kasiṇa.
prerequisites: fourth (fifth) jhāna on a kasiṇa with mastery

name: Perception of repulsiveness in nutriment (āhāre paṭikūlasaññā)
method_summary: Reviewing food in ten aspects — going, seeking, using, secretion, receptacle, uncooked, cooked, fruit, outflow, smearing — until it appears repulsive; reaches access and removes craving for flavours.

name: Defining the four elements (catudhātuvavatthāna)
method_summary: Discerning the body as earth, water, fire and air — briefly for the quick-witted, or by forty-two aspects; the perception of a being disappears; reaches access; in the Pa-Auk tradition by twelve characteristics, leading to the sight of material groups.

equivalents.note: the sutta contemplation of elements (MN 10) (U36)

name: The fourfold purity of virtue (catupārisuddhi-sīla)
method_summary: Restraint by the Pātimokkha, restraint of the sense faculties, purification of livelihood, and use of the requisites with reflection.

name: The thirteen ascetic practices (dhutaṅga)
method_summary: Voluntary austerities undertaken for effacement: refuse-rag robes, three robes only, alms-food, house-to-house alms, one session, bowl-food, refusing later food, forest dwelling, tree-root, open air, charnel ground, any bed, the sitter's practice; each has strict, medium and mild grades.

warnings.text: They suit the greedy and deluded temperaments; undertaken with the wish to be admired they become a basis of evil desire.

name: The refuse-rag wearer's practice (pamsukulikaṅga)
method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the refuse-rag wearer's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

name: The triple-robe wearer's practice (tecivarikaṅga)
method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the triple-robe wearer's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the alms-food eater's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the house-to-house seeker's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the one-sessioner's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the bowl-food eater's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the later-food refuser's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the forest-dweller's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the tree-root dweller's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the open-air dweller's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the charnel-ground dweller's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the any-bed user's practice, undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

name: The sitter's practice (not lying down) (nesajjikaṅga)
method_summary: One of the thirteen ascetic practices: the sitter's practice (not lying down), undertaken by formal resolve and kept in strict, medium or mild form.

warnings.text: To be undertaken only with health and a teacher's approval; broken by the conditions stated for each (general statement).

notes: Name slug in Pali without diacritics. The sitter's practice is flagged restricted as a prolonged sleep-deprivation austerity (summary only).

name: The ten skills in absorption (appanā-kosalla)
method_summary: Making the basis clean, balancing the faculties (faith with wisdom, energy with concentration; mindfulness everywhere), skill in the sign, exerting, restraining and encouraging the mind when needed, equanimity when it runs evenly, avoiding distracted people, cultivating concentrated people, resolving upon concentration.

name: The five masteries of jhāna (vasī)
method_summary: Practising adverting to, attaining, resolving the duration of, emerging from and reviewing a jhāna wherever, whenever and for as long as one wishes, before going on to the next.

name: Developing the direct knowledges (abhiññā)
method_summary: From the fourth jhāna on the kasiṇas, after taming the mind in fourteen ways (in order, reverse order, skipping kasiṇas and jhānas, etc.), the meditator resolves with the direct-knowledge consciousness to produce supernormal powers, the divine ear and eye, knowledge of minds and recollection of past lives — summary only.
prerequisites: mastery of all eight attainments on the eight kasiṇas

warnings.text: The worldling's supernormal power is hard to maintain, like an infant lying on its back or young corn, broken by a trifle; it is an impediment to insight and should be severed by one who seeks insight.

notes: Recorded as a summary with the text's own warning; no operational detail.

name: Defining mentality-materiality (nāmarūpa-pariccheda)
method_summary: Purification of view: discerning the jhāna factors and their associates (calm vehicle) or the four elements (insight vehicle) by characteristic, function, manifestation and proximate cause, until only mentality-materiality is seen and no being or person.

name: Discerning conditions (paccaya-pariggaha)
method_summary: Purification by overcoming doubt: seeking the causes of mentality-materiality (ignorance, craving, clinging, kamma, nutriment) in the three periods, like a physician seeking a disease's origin; in the Pa-Auk tradition by directly discerning past and future lives.

name: Comprehension by groups (kalāpa-sammasana)
method_summary: Applying the three characteristics to formations grouped by aggregate, period and so on — 'impermanent in the sense of destruction, painful in the sense of terror, not-self in the sense of coreless' — the beginning of full understanding as investigation.

name: Attainment of fruition (phala-samāpatti)
method_summary: A noble person enters the fruition of his attainment, with nibbāna as object, resolving on its duration, for a pleasant abiding here and now.

name: Attainment of cessation (nirodha-samāpatti)
method_summary: A non-returner or arahant with the eight attainments emerges from each attainment in turn and contemplates it with insight up to the base of nothingness, performs the four preliminary duties, attains the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception and then cessation, for up to seven days — summary only.

warnings.text: Belongings not resolved upon may be destroyed; the limit of one's life-span must be reviewed first (the story of the elder Mahānāga).

name: Ledi Sayadaw's lay insight method
method_summary: Establishing mindfulness of breathing (or of the body), then contemplating the four elements, feelings and the aggregates as impermanent, suffering and not-self, supported by study of the Abhidhamma manuals; offered to laypeople.

name: Noting (the Mahāsi method)
method_summary: Making a light mental note of every object as it arises — 'rising', 'falling', 'thinking', 'hearing', 'pain', 'intending' — in sitting, walking and all daily activities, to build continuous mindfulness and momentary concentration and see arising and passing.
signs_of_progress: the insight knowledges in sequence (Progress of Insight)

warnings.text: Lights, rapture and other experiences at the stage of arising and passing are to be noted, not taken for attainment.

name: Noting the rising and falling of the abdomen
method_summary: The primary object of Mahāsi sitting practice: the movement of the abdomen, noted as 'rising' and 'falling', to which attention returns after noting other objects.

name: Walking meditation with noting
method_summary: Walking slowly back and forth, noting the phases of each step (lifting, pushing, dropping) with increasing precision; alternated with sitting periods.

name: Body scanning (observation of sensations)
method_summary: Moving attention systematically through the body, part by part, from head to feet and back, observing whatever sensation is present — gross or subtle — with equanimity and the understanding of impermanence; later sweeping the body in free flow.
prerequisites: three days of mindfulness of respiration

warnings.text: Practise only within a course under an authorized teacher; do not mix with other techniques (the tradition's own rule).

name: The ten-day Vipassana course (Goenka)
method_summary: A residential course in noble silence: taking refuge and the five precepts, surrender to the teacher and the technique; mindfulness of respiration at the nostrils for three and a half days; body scanning from the fourth day; loving-kindness on the last day; recorded evening discourses; given free on donation.

name: The Sunlun method
method_summary: A sitting begins with strong, deliberate breathing to build concentration, after which the breathing is released and attention is fixed on the touch sensation at the nostrils and then on all bodily sensations, especially pain, which is watched without moving until it dissolves — summary only.

warnings.text: Taught under a teacher's supervision; the forceful breathing is not to be improvised (general statement; the tradition's own wording not available here).

notes: No breath counts or durations recorded.

name: Discerning material groups (Pa-Auk)
method_summary: With concentration from four-elements meditation or jhāna, the body is seen to break into tiny particles (kalāpa); each kind is analysed into its elements (at least eight), across the six doors and four origins, before mentality is discerned.

name: The Mogok method
method_summary: Study of dependent origination with a chart, then contemplation of the arising and passing of each consciousness and feeling as it occurs (mind and feeling contemplation).

name: Recitation of 'buddho'
method_summary: Silent repetition of 'buddho' — alone or 'bud-' with the in-breath and '-dho' with the out-breath — until the mind settles; then the word is dropped and the breath or body is contemplated.

equivalents.note: a form of recollection of the Buddha used as a concentration word

name: Dhutaṅga wandering (tudong)
method_summary: Wandering alone or in small groups through forests and mountains, dwelling under a klot (umbrella tent) in forests, caves and charnel grounds, living on alms and practising meditation, facing fear and hardship.

equivalents.note: the Thai forest form of the ascetic practices

name: Ajahn Lee's breath meditation (Method 2)
method_summary: Begin with 'buddho' and a few long breaths; observe and adjust the breath until comfortable; attend to its resting spots (nose tip, middle of the head, palate, base of the throat, breastbone, navel); spread the breath energy through the whole body; keep the mind still in the breath and develop discernment.

equivalents.note: a development of mindfulness of breathing working with breath energy in the body

name: Dhammakāya meditation (Wat Paknam method)
method_summary: The mind is brought down through a series of bases (nostril, eye-corner, centre of the head, palate, throat, navel level) to the seventh base at the centre of the body, while visualizing a clear crystal sphere and repeating 'sammā arahaṃ', until a bright sphere and then successive inner bodies appear.
notes: From secondary knowledge; exact list of bases not verified.

name: Installing the raptures in the body (borān kammaṭṭhāna)
method_summary: After preliminary rites and a formal request to the teacher, the meditator induces the five kinds of rapture in order, each fixed at a prescribed place in the body with Pali syllables, before proceeding to further qualities — summary only.

name: Protective chanting (paritta)
method_summary: Chanting of protective suttas (e.g. Ratana, Mettā, Khandha, Āṭānāṭiya) by monks, often with a thread and water; in the commentarial tradition effective through the truth and loving-kindness of the texts.
notes: U37 contributes only the commentarial-ritual usage; U36 owns the sutta sources.

name: Chanting the Abhidhamma at funerals
method_summary: In Thailand and Burma monks chant the opening passages (mātikā) of the seven Abhidhamma books at funerals and memorials, for the benefit of the departed and the listeners.
notes: Practice attested in Thai and Burmese custom; no text source recorded.

name: Dedication of merit (pattidāna)
method_summary: Sharing merit with the departed and others after meritorious deeds; the Kathāvatthu denies that the gift itself passes to the other world, while the practice of dedication continues.

name: Supporting the dying with wholesome objects
method_summary: Relatives and monks help the dying recollect their good deeds, chant, and bring offerings or Buddha-images into view, so that a wholesome kamma or sign becomes the object of the last cognitive process, which conditions rebirth.
notes: Popular practice resting on the Abhidhamma account of death; text support is the doctrine, not an injunction.
